# EventFlow — Project Knowledge Hub

> Official public knowledge base for the EventFlow project.
> Last updated: 2026-11-13.
> Language: Russian.
> Documentation status: actively maintained.

## Project

EventFlow is a digital invitation and event management service.

This repository contains publicly available project context, product documentation, architecture summaries, historical audit registry, database documentation, agreed decisions, and safe handoff materials.

It is a public knowledge hub. Full working specifications and documentation remain in private project repositories.

## Main Priority — Release Two Working Prototypes

The current top priority is to release two usable demonstration products as quickly as possible:

1. New Year invitations — first, as the more compact prototype.
2. Wedding invitations — second, on the shared base, with guest/family personalization and the QR scenario.

The release sequence is:

- shared functional base;
- New Year template and complete invitation/RSVP flow;
- wedding template and required wedding-specific features;
- end-to-end verification of both prototypes.

Do not let documentation, infrastructure, automation, or nonessential features delay these releases. Reuse working code. Implement only what the immediate prototype scenario requires. Do not build a universal editor or repeat audits without a concrete reason.

Public summary of the release plan: [DEMO_RELEASE_PLAN.md](DEMO_RELEASE_PLAN.md). The full working plan and detailed agreed decisions are kept in private project materials.

Read these documents in the following order:

3. [PROJECT_STATUS.md](PROJECT_STATUS.md) — current verified status, Demo limitations, and immediate next actions.
4. [DEMO_RELEASE_PLAN.md](DEMO_RELEASE_PLAN.md) — public summary of the two-prototype release plan.

## Important Rules for AI Agents

- Read AI_CONTEXT.md, AI_HANDOFF.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md, and DEMO_RELEASE_PLAN.md before starting work.
- Treat prototype release as the main priority; prefer the shortest safe path to a working user scenario.
- Inspect relevant existing documentation before proposing another audit.
- Do not repeat completed audits without a specific reason.
- Do not treat historical SQL files as the current production schema.
- Never run the initial SQL archive blindly against the active database.
- Distinguish verified facts, agreed decisions, preliminary decisions, hypotheses, implemented features, and tested scenarios.
- Do not claim that a feature is implemented merely because it is described in product documentation or has a UI element.
- Do not change agreed architectural or commercial decisions without discussing the change.
- Update relevant documentation after significant project changes.
- Do not publish secrets, credentials, tokens, private customer data, or other confidential information.
- Before editing a GitHub file, fetch its latest content and SHA; after editing, fetch it again and verify the result.
- Make small sequential changes. After each change, provide one concrete verification step and wait for confirmation.

## Public Source Code — Demo

Public demo repository:

https://github.com/PelzA83/eventflow-demo

Demo start page:

https://pelza83.github.io/eventflow-demo/demo.html

The current public demonstration uses a SharedWorker and in-memory session data. It is not a persistent backend and must not be described as permanent storage or as connected to the production Supabase database.

Open the guest and organizer demo pages through the start page so they receive the same demo session context. See PROJECT_STATUS.md for verified functionality and known limitations.

The public repository is a demonstration copy, not a mirror of the private working codebase. It does not grant access to private source code, specifications, or the production database.

## Public and Private Repositories

https://pelza83.github.io/eventflow-project-hub/

Private working application and specifications repository:

PelzA83/EventFlow

Private additional documentation repository:

https://github.com/PelzA83/eventflow-project-docs

The private repositories are not publicly accessible. Do not assume their contents can be opened without authorization. The additional documentation repository and the main application/specifications repository are separate repositories.

## Documentation Limitations

This hub contains curated public summaries, not a complete mirror of private project materials.

The presence of a document does not necessarily mean that the described functionality has been implemented or recently verified.

For the latest confirmed state, consult PROJECT_STATUS.md and check the actual application and database when necessary. The public Demo has temporary session storage; do not infer persistence from a successful in-session test.
